requirement:
Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.

The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
rationale:
The reviewed tests in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]` cover each obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`. Selection, freshness, and the exception mechanics are cited requirements, so I only checked that the threshold tests apply them.

**80% target on exact counts, per file**
- `exact_per_file_threshold_and_partial_functions` calls `threshold(79_999, 100_000)` and asserts it fails, although it would display as 80.0%.
- It asserts that `threshold(80_000, 100_000)` passes and that `threshold(0, 0)` fails.
- Through the report, it asserts 4/5 passes at exactly 80%.
- It asserts `driver.rs` at 0/1 fails even though another file is at 100%.
- It asserts `driver.rs` at 7/10 fails even though the two-file average is 85%.
- That second case also covers "not average file percentages".

**No 80% target per function**
- `a_function_below_eighty_percent_needs_no_exception_when_its_file_passes` has a function at 1/3 inside a file at 10/12. It asserts the report passes and lists no accepted exceptions.

**Union counts, child processes, and filtered runs**
- `children_and_filtered_runs_contribute_to_the_same_union` splits executions between a parent and a child process, and asserts 5/5.
- It then adds a later all-zero record from a second test and asserts 5/5 still holds, so one positive count anywhere covers a line.

**Selection and freshness within the active configuration**
- `stale_missing_legacy_and_uncertain_history_cannot_use_older_success` asserts a record from another configuration is excluded and does not break a passing report.
- It asserts a newer attempt with missing coverage is not rescued by an older success.
- It asserts a newer attempt lacking function attribution is reported.
- It asserts stale source is reported as stale coverage.
- It asserts an unreadable run record is reported as unable to establish latest-per-test.

**Exception evidence**
- `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution` checks several cases:
  - A file exception passes the file at 0/1 but does not waive its function, so the report fails.
  - Accepted file and function citations pass the report, with the exceptions listed separately.
  - An accepted file exception covers a file that is not measured at all.
  - A review with determination false fails the report.
  - A review that accepts a `{fixme}` is rejected.
- `missing_and_stale_explanations_fail_the_report` covers a missing review, changed citations, and a changed outline input.
- `function_explanations_never_transfer_to_other_functions_or_the_file` checks that an exception on one function does not excuse another function or the file.

**Unmeasured files, files with no obligations, and parse failures**
- `unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear` asserts a file with no executable obligations (`struct S; trait T { fn declaration(); }`) reports "no executable obligations — pass" and the report passes.
- In the same test, a file containing `fn missing() {}` with no recorded lines reports "not measured — FAIL". This enforces "absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish no obligations".
- The same test asserts a parse failure fails the report.
- `measured_file_threshold_remains_checked_when_source_parsing_fails` asserts that a measured file in a nested directory that fails to parse still gets a "below 80%" failure plus the parse error.
- `default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not` asserts a `#[cfg(any())]` function is reported as not measured, and checks `inventory` directly on declarations, macro invocations, and derives.

**Scope**
- Excluding the root `vendor` directory while including `src/vendor` is checked by `post_suite_scope_excludes_root_vendor_but_includes_source_vendor`. It carries a `check.scope` marking rather than a marking for this requirement, but that matches the separate scope requirement.

I found no requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.

text: :::{req} check.threshold
Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.
The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Outline inputs recorded from selected search snippets under {cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs` MUST count alongside mandatory inputs and additional reads. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
:::{req} index.summary
Saved execution-coverage checks compute line coverage from the union of
instrumented file-and-line locations in the selected fresh records under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, including child processes.
Each location counts once in the denominator and is covered when any selected
record has a positive execution count. Percentages use these union counts,
rather than averaging process reports. A selection containing no instrumented
lines, or incomplete measurements, is unavailable under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`; otherwise absent
file or function measurements remain subject to their coverage obligations.
:::{req} index.selection
Saved execution-coverage checks select the most recent recorded attempt
for each nextest binary and test name within the instrumented configuration
of the most recently started recorded attempt. Most recent refers to when an
attempt started, including failed or interrupted attempts. A newer filtered
run updates only tests it executes, leaving other compatible records available.
A newer attempt with missing or unreadable coverage is unavailable and does
not fall back to an older success. Incompatible configurations under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration` are excluded.
Selection uses recorded metadata without building or executing tests.
:::{req} index.freshness
Only records whose captured source inputs match the current source and
whose build configurations are compatible contribute counts to saved
execution-coverage checks under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`. Invalidated records or
records of unknown compatibility are identified as stale or unavailable and
excluded from combined totals. Per-process reports and matching captured
source remain retained until their build artifacts are removed.
